text:
elaine: Heads-up — I spotted a mismatch in the API ref for POST /v1/generate. The model enum in the schema shows snake_case (e.g. `redwood_1`) but examples / the JS SDK use kebab/camel variants (e.g. `redwood-1` / `redwood1`). This makes the client-side validator throw in the browser.

samir: Which file/section? can you paste the snippet?

elaine: Sure — from api-ref.json schema section: 
```json
"model": {
  "type": "string",
  "enum": ["redwood_1", "redwood_2"]
}
```
and in examples we have: 
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-1",
  "prompt": "Say hi"
}
```

kevin: Oof. That explains the integration test flakiness I saw. The runtime accepts both aliases via routing, but our generated JS client does strict enum checks.

docs-bot: linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1715 — added failing example and unit test (auto).

carla: Proposed fix options:
- Update schema enum to include both variants (backcompat)
- Normalize examples to canonical enum and add note about aliases
- Make JS SDK relax enum check and map aliases at runtime

samir: I prefer normalizing docs + adding alias note. Changing SDK behavior is riskier and will need a release.

elaine: Agreed. I can open a small PR to update all examples and the example snippets in the SDK readme. Will also add a migration note under "Breaking changes" so users know we standardized values.

kevin: If you do that, can you also check the response schema for `choices[].metadata`? The docs say `nullable: false` but the runtime sometimes returns null for empty metadata map which breaks TypeScript typings.

elaine: Good catch — here's the response excerpt: 
```json
"choices": {
  "type": "array",
  "items": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "text": { "type": "string" },
      "metadata": { "type": "object", "nullable": false }
    }
  }
}
```
But we actually emit `metadata: null` for legacy models.

carla: For responses I'd prefer making `metadata` nullable in the schema and adding a short migration note: "Older models may return null; prefer `choice.metadata ?? {}`". That keeps client code safe.

samir: Sounds good. So action items: 
- elaine: update all examples for `model` to canonical enum (redwood_1 etc.), add alias note.
- elaine: patch response schema to set `metadata` nullable and add migration snippet.
- kevin: once PR is up, run the JS SDK unit tests and integration smoke tests.
- carla: I'll review and add a docs-bot check to warn on enum/example mismatches.

elaine: I'll open the PR in ~30m and add both changes in one docs patch. Ping me here if I missed any example files.

kevin: Thanks — also add a one-line changelog entry under docs/changelog.md so customers see the normalization. :thumbsup:

docs-bot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1716 — includes example normalization, response schema nullable change, and migration snippet. CI: docs-lint / examples-check running.

samir: Nice, I'll kick off the JS SDK nightly with that branch once CI passes.

elaine: Updated the PR per carla's comments (added alias note and explicit example mapping). Ready for final review.

carla: Reviewing now. If green, merge and backfill the public changelog.

kevin: Post-merge, I'll bump the SDK typings patch to accept nullable metadata and release a patch.

samir: Thanks everyone. Small thread but yeah this was the source of a few stray errors in staging.

elaine: thanks — closing the loop once merged.
